Producer review feedback on CG-0MS934XSL00453HF (raised selection feature, currently in_review): when a card raises, the selection highlight does not raise with it. Additionally the raise slider should go to a maximum of 180px with a default of 60px.

Root cause: in HandView.updateSelectionTints(), applySelectionRaise(true) runs BEFORE the tint loop, so on first selection the raise tween starts before the tint overlay exists — the overlay is created at the resting position and is not in the tween targets, so the card raises while the highlight stays behind. Hover pointerover/pointerout also destroy+recreate the overlay, which can orphan it mid-tween.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Regression tests written FIRST (TDD): animated-path first-selection overlay is included in the raise tween targets; hover repaint reuses the overlay in place; reduced-motion first-selection overlay ends at the raised position.
2. The selection highlight overlay always ends at the raised position on first selection (animated and reduced-motion).
3. GymHandPileScene raise slider: RAISE_MAX = 180, RAISE_DEFAULT = 60; reset() restores the default; Controls help text updated.
4. HandView setSelectionLift() API default remains 0 (opt-in) — backward compatible.
5. npm run build succeeds and all HandView + Gym unit tests pass.
data.title: Gym Hand & Pile: selection highlight raises with the card; raise slider max 180 / default 60

## Summary

Research spike to determine the client-side follow-detection mechanism for the "Follow us on Steam" incentive. The Steam client SDK has no direct "user follows this game's store page" call, so candidates must be verified before committing. This feature produces the decision-gate report that F4 depends on.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A report documents and evaluates each candidate: `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing(<developer account>)` (client-side, no backend), Steam Web API `IPlayerService` (game-page follow, needs server + publisher API key), and any other client-side candidates discovered.
- [ ] The report states a recommendation and flags the UX impact of each candidate (e.g. follows developer account vs game page).
- [ ] The recommendation is confirmed with the user (decision gate) and recorded in this item before F4 implementation commits to a mechanism.
- [ ] Any unknown (e.g. whether a server component is acceptable) is surfaced as an open question with options, not silently assumed.

## Minimal Implementation

- Prototype a minimal probe using the Steamworks SDK against a real Steam account (dev environment with Steam running).
- Research Steamworks SDK docs / community reports for `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing` semantics.
- Write findings to the work item as a structured report (markdown), including a decision recommendation.
- No production code committed in this feature.

## Prototype/Experiment

Success = a clear recommendation with evidence (docs/community/experiment) that the implementer can act on without re-research.

## Dependencies

- Parent blocked-by CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW (Electron launcher) — launcher must exist to run Steamworks in-app.

## Deliverables

- Decision-gate report (in work item comments).
- Confirmed mechanism choice.

# Intake Brief: Enable Main Street Expansion of Playing Area

## Problem Statement

Main Street currently has a single fixed 2×5 street (10 slots) with no ability to expand the playing field. The player should be able to zoom out at any time to reveal a larger 2D grid of streets, where each cell is a 2×5 street. Corner slots between streets are shared — one card serves all four adjacent streets, with normal adjacency rules.

## Users & User Stories

- **As a player**, I want to zoom out and explore neighbouring streets so that I can place more businesses and grow my empire beyond the initial 10-slot grid.
- **As a player**, I want shared corner plots between streets so that strategically placed businesses create cross-street synergy bonuses.
- **As a player**, I want the zoom to work like a map — smooth camera movement that reveals streets organically without gating or milestones.
- **As a game engine developer**, I want the grid system to be unbounded (or at least large enough to support extended play) so the game doesn't end prematurely when all streets are full.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Camera system**: A zoom/pan camera system is implemented for Main Street, allowing the player to zoom out to reveal neighbouring streets. The zoom is controlled by the player (e.g. scroll wheel or button), not gated by milestones.
2. **Grid topology**: The street grid is represented as a 2D lattice where each cell is a 2×5 street. Corner slots (where streets meet at the corners of adjacent 2×5 grids) are shared — one card slot serves the shared position, and the card is adjacent to neighbours in all four streets per normal adjacency rules.
3. **Adjacency & synergy**: The adjacency resolver (`MainStreetAdjacency.ts`) is updated to compute correct 8-way Chebyshev adjacency across street cells, including shared corner slots. Synergy bonuses and income calculations work correctly for cards on expanded streets and shared corners.
4. **Rendering**: All street cells within the current camera viewport are rendered. Cards placed on expanded or shared slots display and interact correctly. Unrevealed streets outside the current zoom level are not rendered.
5. **Save/Load**: The expanded grid state (all placed cards, including shared corner cards, and current zoom/camera position) serializes and deserializes correctly.

## Constraints

- The zoom is **always available** — no gating by milestones, turns, or resources.
- The grid is **conceptually unbounded** (at minimum, support at least a 3×3 or 5×5 grid of streets). Practically, the grid could grow dynamically as the player zooms out further.
- Corner plots are **shared between streets**: one card slot, one card, normal adjacency rules (8-way Chebyshev) apply — the card counts as a neighbour to all adjacent slots across all streets it touches.
- The existing `GRID_SIZE = 10`, `STREET_COLS = 5`, `STREET_ROWS = 2` constants and the flat 10-slot array must be refactored to support multi-street topology.
- Must preserve deterministic seed-based gameplay and save/load compatibility.
- Existing adjacency/synergy/Income systems must continue working without modification to core logic — only the coordinate/adjacency mapping layer changes.

## Existing State

- **Single street**: `GRID_SIZE = 10`, `STREET_COLS = 5`, `STREET_ROWS = 2` (from `MainStreetConstants.ts` and `MainStreetCards.ts`).
- **Flat array**: `streetGrid` is `(BusinessCard | CommunitySpaceCard | null)[]` with row-major indexing.
- **Adjacency**: `MainStreetAdjacency.ts` — `toGridPosition()` maps flat index → {x, y} using `STREET_COLS = 5`; `neighbors()` computes 8-way Chebyshev distance within the 10-slot boundary.
- **Rendering**: `MainStreetRenderer.ts` and `MainStreetLayoutAdapter.ts` position 10 slots in two rows, hardcoded layout.
- **No camera system**: Phaser camera is not used for street navigation; the game uses a fixed viewport.
- **SpatialRules**: Core engine provides `Grid<T>`, `neighbors()`, `shortestPath()` (`@core-engine/SpatialRules`) — reusable for multi-street topology.

## Desired Change

- Introduce a 2D street-cell grid where each cell is a 2×5 street (10 slots).
- Add a camera/zoom system to navigate the grid.
- Refactor the adjacency resolver to work with the 2D grid, computing correct neighbours across street cells and shared corners.
- Update rendering to draw all visible street cells within the viewport.
- Update state serialization to include the full grid and camera position.

## Key Files (Predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts` — Refactor `STREET_COLS/ROWS` into per-street-cell dimensions; add grid dimension constants.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — Update `GRID_SIZE` to a dynamic value; remove hard-coded 10-slot assumption.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — Change `streetGrid` from flat array to 2D grid structure; add camera/zoom state.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` — Refactor `toGridPosition()`, `neighbors()` to compute positions on the 2D street-cell grid; handle shared corner slots.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — Update rendering loop to iterate over visible street cells; add camera transform.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetLayoutAdapter.ts` — Update layout calculations for multi-street grid.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — Integrate camera control (zoom/pan input), wire up rendering and adjacency changes.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — Update drop-zone and click-target logic for expanded grid.

## Related Work

- **CG-0MM4RDIMT1HLP2DE**: Main Street GDD Review and Consolidation (parent epic)
- **CG-0MM5ZG7071KO7PVG**: Adjacency & Spatial Rules (core engine spatial system)
- **CG-0MQKA533D003P55Y**: Gym: SpatialRules demo scene (Grid + pathfinding)
- **CG-0MM4RG1GM0SRVENC**: Main Street PRD Milestone 6 — Engine Component Extraction
- **CG-0MM4R9UJF1DGI0ZF**: Main Street (parent epic)
- **CG-0MPENWRBO0051ZQT**: Port Main Street to SLL (UI layout modernisation)
- **CG-0MT5Y1X5T001M4S6**: This item — Enable Main Street expansion of playing area

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- **Q1**: What triggers the grid expansion? — **A**: No gating — player can zoom out at any time. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2**: How does "zoom" work visually and mechanically? — **A**: Like a map — camera zoom reveals pre-defined streets on a larger 2D grid. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3**: What does "corner plots shared with each edge" mean for gameplay? — **A**: Yes, shared corner slot counts as adjacent to neighbours in both streets. One card slot, one card, normal adjacency rules apply. Source: interactive reply.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MQU3AREL0099R1I** – Main Street refined layout: column-based right panel, wider market/street (completed)
- **CG-0MLVOTXVS1IEK03X** – Migrate GolfScene layout to 1280x720 (completed)
- **CG-0MO4LWWQY008SWRK** – Thumbnail: canonical fixture + automated generation (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: ability, able, add, allowing, always (+184 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: ability, able, acceptance, add, adjacency (+159 more)
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` — matched: 0mm4rdimt1hlp2de, ability, able, acceptance, add (+156 more)

# Feature: Deterministic Banking AI Tests (BankingGreedyStrategy)

## Summary
Expand `tests/main-street/ai-banking-strategy.test.ts` to contract `BankingGreedyStrategy` (distinct class, not `GreedyStrategy`) for hoard/spend/cap/legality/difficulty; leave Greedy baseline untouched.

## Target Outcome
Deterministic, fast unit tests prove `BankingGreedyStrategy` deliberately hoards vs spends correctly and respects legality, before implementation lands.

## Definition of Done
- Suite imports `BankingGreedyStrategy` (name === 'BankingGreedy', implements MainStreetAiStrategy) alongside unchanged Greedy/Random.
- Cases: (a) hoards (end-turn with actionsRemaining>0) when an unaffordable high-value hand/market target exists, (b) spends when no valuable unaffordable target, (c) at bankedActions==2 returns spend (bank value 0), (d) respects enumerateLegalActions legality (no illegal action emitted), (e) difficulty scaling — Easy spends where Hard hoards on same state.
- Existing ai-action-budget + monte-carlo tests remain green (or drift documented).
- `npx vitest run --project unit tests/main-street/ai-banking-strategy.test.ts` passes.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. New suite targets `BankingGreedyStrategy`; GreedyStrategy and RandomStrategy remain importable/unchanged.
2. Deterministic hoard vs spend vs cap vs legality cases covered (a–d above).
3. Difficulty scaling test: same state, Easy spends where Hard hoards (or quantified threshold difference documented).
4. No regression in existing ai-action-budget / monte-carlo tests (or documented drift).

## Minimal Implementation
- Retarget/create helper makeState({hand, market, coins, banked, difficulty/config}) in tests/main-street/ai-banking-strategy.test.ts.
- Table-driven tests for cases above; include helper to build MainStreetState with hand/market/business+upgrade/event cards and bankedActions.
- Run: `npx vitest run --project unit tests/main-street/ai-banking-strategy.test.ts`.

## Dependencies
None (test-first — blocks F2).

## Deliverables
- `tests/main-street/ai-banking-strategy.test.ts` (expanded/retargeted)
- Passing unit run for touched file

## Key Files
- `tests/main-street/ai-banking-strategy.test.ts`
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts`
- `tests/main-street/ai-action-budget.test.ts`

## Constraints
- Main Street only; no core-engine changes.
- Do not modify GreedyStrategy behaviour in this slice — tests define the contract it must satisfy in F2.

# Feature: Design architecture & extraction script with history (F1)

Decide the target multi-repo layout, enumerate assets, and build the history-preserving extraction script. Full history preservation via `git filter-repo` is required (per producer).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Architecture decision recorded: core repo contents (`src/core-engine`, `src/card-system`, `src/rule-engine`, `src/ui`, `src/ai`, `src/balance-cards`, Gym, launcher shell `src/ui/GameSelectorScene` + `src/ui/createCardGame`, `electron/`, shared configs), game repo layout as sibling `tce-<game>` dirs, launcher composition via `configs/*.json` presets and a Vite discovery plugin.
2. History-preservation strategy confirmed as `git filter-repo` and the exact filter commands / script are documented and dry-run verified.
3. Asset ownership enumerated case-by-case for `public/assets/` — audit of `public/assets/CREDITS.md` and per-game usage; decision table committed (which assets stay in core vs move with a game).
4. Extraction script `scripts/extract-repos.sh` (or equivalent) produces the core-engine directory/repo and 8 per-game scaffolds from the current monorepo state with history preserved; dry-run output is verifiable.

## Technical Notes

- Use `git filter-repo` (not subtree/manual squashed history) — producer confirmed full history preservation.
- Enumerate shared vs per-game assets before any moves; thumbnail assets are per-game (each game provides its own).
- Sibling layout: core at `../tableau-card-engine-core` relative to each `tce-<game>` sibling.

## Key Files

- `scripts/extract-repos.sh` (new)
- `docs/extract-architecture.md` or decision record (new)
- `public/assets/CREDITS.md`
- `public/assets/**`

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: Full history preservation? A (producer, this session): yes, via `git filter-repo`.
- Q: Asset ownership? A (producer, this session): enumerate in F1, decide case-by-case.
- Q: Dynamic discovery approach? A (producer, this session): convention (GAME_INFO per game) is fine; per-game thumbnails.
- Q: Post-build dynamic addition? A (producer, this session): rebuild sufficient for now; Electron runtime plugin is a follow-up (core-version compatibility required).

## Failure Signature

- Test name: browser full-suite contention flake (upgrade-drag-drop / HelpPanelLayering / expanded-viewport)
- Failing commit: (not available)
- CI job: (not available)

## Evidence

- Short stderr/stdout excerpt (first 1k characters):

```
Timed out waiting for card placed / colorDistance(maxDist).toBeGreaterThan(15) — under full-suite concurrent load; all three files pass when run in isolation (verified repeatedly)
```

## Root Cause Analysis

Three Main Street browser tests pass individually but fail under full-suite browser load. The shared Chromium process exhausts Phaser 4's CanvasPool GPU contexts after many sequential game create/destroy cycles (41 Main Street browser tests in the suite). The tutorial E2E tests solve this with `drainCanvasPool()` in their `destroyGame` helper; the regular browser tests lack this cleanup.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The three failing browser test files pass under full-suite browser load (not just in isolation): `tests/main-street/upgrade-drag-drop.browser.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/HelpPanelLayering.browser.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/expanded-viewport.browser.test.ts`.
2. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes.
3. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Key Files

- `tests/main-street/upgrade-drag-drop.browser.test.ts` — drag-drop test (timeout on 'card placed')
- `tests/main-street/HelpPanelLayering.browser.test.ts` — HelpPanel z-ordering test
- `tests/main-street/expanded-viewport.browser.test.ts` — expanded viewport test
- `tests/helpers/main-street-tutorial-e2e.ts` — reference `destroyGame` / `drainCanvasPool` for the fix pattern

## Suggested Triage Steps

1. Verify flakiness: rerun CI/test locally once.
2. If reproducible, assign to `Build` and route for triage.
3. If flaky, tag `flaky` and route to flaky-test queue.

## Suspected Owner

Build (confidence: 0.0, reason: no owner inference available)
